CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: lock access to cmdq_flush cmdq_flush is asserted in mtk_drm_crtc_atomic_flush() to indicate that pending changes have been copied into the cmdq_pending* fields. At the next line irq, mtk_crtc_target_line_irq() will then schedule cmdq_work, which calls mtk_drm_crtc_commit_cmdq() to create a cmdq_rec, fill it with the changes in the cmdq_pending*, and clear cmdq_flush. Currently, however, mtk_drm_crtc_atomic_flush() asserts cmdq_flush before it has completed copying pending state into cmdq_pending*. This creates a race, where a subsequent line irq may schedule cmdq_work, and mtk_drm_crtc_commit_cmdq() may get a chance to create a cmdq_rec with an incomplete update. Furthermore, cmdq_work() could race with a second mtk_drm_crtc_atomic_flush(), which would, similarly, either overwrite some of the previous cmdq_pending* fields, and/or have its pending updates lost if mtk_drm_crtc_commit_cmdq() clears its assertion of cmdq_flush before it was seen by the line irq, leading to a lost update. Fix this race condition by adding a mutex around the accesses to the cmdq_pending* fields in both atomic_flush and commit_cmdq to make production and consumption of pending changes atomic. Signed-off-by: Bibby Hsieh <bibby.hsieh@mediatek.com> BUG=chrome-os-partner:50740 TEST=Play 1080p 60fps video on oak-rev5 over 14 hours. (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PlhFkShzc_0) Change-Id: Ie1351a65f92f7ae2d7df288bbd7676c9c072388b Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/331001 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: Bibby Hsieh <bibby.hsieh@mediatek.com> Reviewed-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/423725 Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: Synchronously flush cmdq when powering off ddp Every cmdq record generates a gce interrupt, even the "stop" command. However, we were always processing these interrupts with the same isr callback, ddp_cmdq_cb. This is dangerous, because ddp_cmdq_cb unconditionally schedules unreference_work. If another cmdq operation is flushed by mtk_drm_crtc_atomic_flush() before the stop command's unreference_work had a chance to run, the unreference_work will unreference the FB that was just flushed (ie, copied from new_fb to old_fb in mtk_drm_crtc_atomic_flush()). This extra unreference will eventually cause problems, since the FB will be freed prematurely. In particular, the FB may be freed before it has been removed from the drm file's active fb list. Common effects of this are crashes due to use-after-free in drm_mode_rmfb() or drm_mode_getresources() as these two functions try to iterate over file_priv->fbs. Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> BUG=chrome-os-partner:50482 TEST=Run the suspend_stress_test on oak-rev5 over 100 times. => No crashes in drm_mode_getresources or drm_rmfb Change-Id: Id5af5153db9c80816cdf4ad71c88d86c097de3e2 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/329085 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Bibby Hsieh <bibby.hsieh@mediatek.com> Reviewed-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/423727 Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: Fix FB reference counting The DRM core takes care of all "synchronous atomic" FB refcounting. However, mediatek drm defers some work that accesses drm_framebuffers, and must therefore keep its own FB references until this work is complete. There are two deferred works: 1) cmdq_work During drm_atomic_commit(), the drm core "atomically" calls mtk_plane_atomic_update() to update each plane's state. This is followed by a call to mtk_drm_crtc_atomic_flush(), which, in theory transfers all pending changes to the hardware for processing. However, the mediatek driver uses the "cmdq" to schedule hardware to perform the an atomic update during the next vblank. Furthermore, there seems to be a limitation that only a single "cmdq_rec" can be scheduled per vblank. Thus, to allow multiple updates per vblank (e.g., a page flip and a cursor update) the driver batches up pending updates and uses the "line" interrupt (which fires at 80% of frame time) to schedule cmdq_work to take the batched updates and send them to the cmdq as a single cmdq_rec. However, since this worker runs after the "atomic update" has completed, it is possible that any framebuffers that were to be used by the batch update may already have been freed. To prevent this, we take a FB reference during mtk_drm_crtc_atomic_flush() to ensure that the FB will still be valid during mtk_drm_crtc_commit_cmdq(). In mtk_drm_crtc_commit_cmdq(), the current onscreen FB becomes the "old" FB, to be unreferenced at the next vblank, and the "new" FB is saved as the new "onscreen" FB, and the "new" FB is cleared. To allow multiple updates to the same plane in a single batch may change the scheduled FB, mtk_drm_crtc_atomic_flush() first checks if there already was a "new" FB, and, if so, drops its reference. Since we now take the FB reference in flush(), we no longer need the reference in mtk_plane_atomic_update(). (2) unreference_work After the cmdq update, a callback schedules unreference_work to drop references on 'old' FBs that are no longer on screen. To ensure there is no race between unreferencing the previous "old" FB and scheduling a new FB update (which may create a new "old" FB), this patch now clears cmdq_busy flag in unreference_work so that cmdq_work will not be scheduled until unreference_work completes. Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> BUG=chrome-os-partner:51218 TEST=build and boot on oak-rev5 TEST=enable DRM debugging & show/hide cursor => Cursor FB # does not increase => Cursor FB refcounts do not increase. TEST=turn panel on/off TEST=suspend_stress_test => No crashes TEST=change resolution on external monitor => No iommu warnings Change-Id: I7372ecf24570bd74f3523564aefcfcccebcc98d9 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/333822 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: Bibby Hsieh <bibby.hsieh@mediatek.com> Tested-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Bibby Hsieh <bibby.hsieh@mediatek.com> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/423749 Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: Fix cmdq_engine_flag to use hardcoded DPI0 pipe Actually "DSI1" could be correct, if someone wanted to use MT8173 with two DSI outputs. However, the current drm/mediatek architecture has hard-coded two display pipes: one for DSI0 and one for DPI0. Furthermore, the cmdq driver also only has hard-coded support matching these two display pipes to two dedicated cmdq threads. Therefore, we have to change it to DPI0 to avoid accidentally selecting the wrong (MISCP) cmdq thread. CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: crtc: Synchronously disable all overlays during crtc->enable During an atomic update, Mediatek DRM disables/enables crtcs and encoders first, and then applies plane state (enable/FB address) changes. On boot, firmware may have enabled some overlays, with an FB that is no longer mapped. Furthermore, drm/mediatek uses active_only, so state changes are only applied to hardware when the corresponding crtc is enabled. In other words, when disabling a CRTC, the CRTC's planes SW state is disabled, but the hardware state is not actually changed at disable time. Thus, like at boot, the overlay hw state will be 'enabled', but the scanout address points to an FB that has already been unmapped. To avoid an iommu fault between when we enable the encoder and when the new plane state is later applied to hardware in both of these cases, explicitly start all overlays in disabled state. The correct plane state for any enabled planes will be applied later in the atomic update. Also, since there is no active scanout anyway, do not wait for a vblank before starting the pipe; rather, just request an immediately synchronous cmdq update. Lastly, since we start the pipes with overlays disabled, we don't need to synchronously turn them off when disabling the crtc. Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> BUG=chrome-os-partner:54665 TEST=boot to ui on elm TEST=HDMI work normal (plug/unplug/replug, display normal, show/hide cursor) TEST=backlight on/off TEST=suspend resume stress test finished 10000 iterations. TEST=chameleon display_HotPlugAtSuspend.extended_unplugged TEST=chameleon display_HotPlugAtSuspend.mirrored_unplugged Change-Id: If06e23d432cd2e55db7b6b31e25f18c51a98bfef Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/362237 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Bibby Hsieh <bibby.hsieh@mediatek.com> Reviewed-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/423960 Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: drm/mediatek: crtc: Remove nofb callback The optional _nofb callback is used to update the display mode of a CRTC without changing anything of the primary plane configuration. The DRM documentation says that since the display pipe is completely off when this function is called, atomic drivers which need hardware to be running before they program the new display mode should not use this hook... Such drivers should instead move all their CRTC setup into the @enable callback. json_utils: add MultiPathJSONRPCServer Currently goofy handles all RPC call in one single instance, which is also the 'state' instance that manages testing state information. So we see many functions defined in either goofy_rpc or state that are not actually related to testing state or goofy. To help modularize goofy, it will be much clear to separate different functions to different instances. Multi-path RPC server can help seperate different RPC instances to different URLs, so each URL can act like a sub RPC server. However, currently in standard library only MultiPathXMLRPCServer is supported. This CL mimics the implementation of MultiPathXMLRPCServer for JSON version. BUG=chromium:658151 TEST=json_utils_unittest.py Change-Id: I22385a5218594cab8704b24f49295b339f160fba Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/445557 Commit-Ready: Shun-Hsing Ou <shunhsingou@chromium.org> Tested-by: Shun-Hsing Ou <shunhsingou@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Pi-Hsun Shih <pihsun@chromium.org>

goofy: implement goofy_server Currently cros.factory.test.state is not only a state data storage, but also a complicated server that: 1. Serves static files for Goofy UI. 2. Handles RPC for Goofy. 3. Partially handles test list status. To achieve this, we see code that inject goofy_rpc functions into state instance to get RPC support, which is not really intuitive. As we'd like to support RPC for Goofy plugins, state server will be too complicated and hard to maintain. In this CL, we implement a goofy_server that is designed to handle above memtioned web request, including serving static files for UI and handling multiple RPC instances. The goal is to make the responsibility of each components more clear: - state: handles shared data. - goofy/goofy_rpc: organizes the system and handles test status. - goofy_server: handles all web requests. - goofy plugins: additional functions for goofy. BUG=chromium:658151 TEST=make test run amd64-generic-goofy toolkit. CHROMIUM: arm64: dts: mt817x: Add GCE node The Global Command Engine (GCE) hardware in the MT817x is used to implement a command queue (CMDQ) which can be programmed to modify device registers upon certain pre-programmed events. It is used in particular for the display controller driver to update display registers during vblank. CHROMIUM: soc: mediatek: SCPSYS: Drop parent/child relationship for mfg domains The mfg power domains do not have a real parent/child relationship, so the current implementation does not reflect reality. Nevertheless the different mfg domains have hardware constraints in that they must be enabled and disabled in a certain order. To make that sure we no longer register the mfg_2d and mfg_async as domains themselves but instead only the mfg domain which then also enables/disabled the other two domains. Note: This is a non-upstreamable CHROMIUM patch, because while it is assumed that this is actually a work-around for an as-yet undiagnosed power sequencing issue in the drm/img-rogue GPU driver. An upstream solution would allow a fully functioning GPU driver to also operate in the following "intermediate" power states: (a) mfg_async (b) mfg_async + mfg_2d This fix in this patch disables these two modes since it always enables/disables all three power domains together, mfg_async/mfg_2d/mfg. For chromeos-4.4, this is a squash of: 4762f11e0c95 CHROMIUM: soc: mediatek: SCPSYS: Drop parent/child relationship for mfg domains 537dccbc8eee BACKPORT: soc: mediatek: SCPSYS: Fix double enabling of regulators CHROMIUM: soc: mediatek: SCPSYS: Fix power off sequence in error path (https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/#/c/448737/) The BACKPORT was actually reverted upstream, since it really just fixes an implementation detail of the CHROMIUM patch - mainline does not have mfg domains, and hence doesn't have a 'double enabling issue'. The BACKPORT's commit message: With CONFIG_PM enabled do not call genpd->power_on manually as this will cause the regulators being turned on once in SCPSYS probe and then again when the genpd core turns on the domains. Instead, call genpd->power_on only with CONFIG_PM disabled and tell the genpd core that the domains are disabled when registered.
